terms.gloss: an analysis, a detailed account of a matter
terms.comment: An unfolding: Cicero’s word for setting out a subject point by point (Lewis & Short). To analyse, explicāre.

terms.gloss: a division into parts, a logical analysis
evidence: Cic. Top. 28: cum rēs ea, quae prōposita est, quasi in membra discerpitur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. ND 3.62: explicātiō fābulārum et ēnōdātiō nōminum

terms.comment: Only of the branch of mathematics.

phrases.latin: Utrum philosophiā dignius, sāgārum superstitiōne ista interpretārī an explicātiōne nātūrae?
phrases.english: Which is worthier of philosophy: to interpret such things by the superstition of fortune-tellers, or by an analysis of nature?

phrases.latin: multumque ad ea, quae quaerimus, explicātiō tua ista prōfēcerit
phrases.english: and that analysis of yours will help a great deal towards what we are looking for

sources: Lewis & Short: explicatio · Lewis & Short: partitio · Lewis & Short: enodatio
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. analysis.
Cicero’s De divinatione, De finibus and De natura deorum checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
Traupman has no word for analysis.
